blogs.title: The Angioedema Masquerade: Dermatomyositis as a Cause of Neck Swelling
blogs.description: Discusses the diagnostic challenge of neck swelling in the ED, highlighting dermatomyositis as a rare but critical differential diagnosis that mimics idiopathic angioedema or deep neck space infections. Focuses on the importance of considering inflammatory myopathy when angioedema workup is negative.

blogs.title: Look at the Nails: Cutaneous Clues to Missed Myositis
blogs.description: A deep dive into the physical examination findings that differentiate dermatomyositis from other causes of edema. Covers subtle signs like nailfold capillaroscopy changes, periungual erythema, and the Holster sign that can be overlooked in acute settings.

blogs.title: SAE1 Positive: Recognizing a High-Risk Dermatomyositis Phenotype
blogs.description: Explores the clinical significance of anti-SAE1 antibodies in dermatomyositis, specifically their strong association with severe dysphagia, interstitial lung disease, and malignancy risk. Helps clinicians understand which patients require aggressive monitoring and screening.

blogs.title: Airway Alert: Dysphagia and Aspiration Risk in Inflammatory Myopathy
blogs.description: Focuses on the management of bulbar involvement in dermatomyositis, including the recognition of severe dysphagia, aspiration pneumonitis, and the necessity for early airway protection and nutritional support via nasogastric tube.

blogs.title: Paraneoplastic Dermatomyositis: When to Screen for Cancer
blogs.description: Reviews the malignancy screening protocols for patients with new-onset dermatomyositis based on IMACS guidelines. Discusses risk stratification factors (age, antibody type, dysphagia) and the appropriate imaging and endoscopic workup.

blogs.title: Rescue Therapy: Managing Severe Dermatomyositis with IVIG and Rituximab
blogs.description: Outlines treatment strategies for severe or refractory dermatomyositis, moving beyond standard steroids to include IVIG, mycophenolate, and rituximab. Discusses the rationale for multi-agent immunosuppression and prophylaxis considerations.
